# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.

13:### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`
14:
15:The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.
16:
17:`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`
18:
19:```yaml
20:# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
21:# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
22:validate:
23:  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
24:  next: load
25:load:
26:  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
27:  next: apply
28:apply:
29:  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
30:  govern: [ transaction ]
31:  next: save
32:save:
33:  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
34:  govern: [ transaction ]
35:  next: respond
36:respond:
37:  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
38:```
39:
40:```java
41:// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
42:public class ValidateOwner {
43:  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
44:    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
45:  }
46:}
47:public class LoadOwner {
48:  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
49:      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
50:    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
51:    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
52:    ownerOut.set(owner);
53:  }
54:}
55:public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
56:  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
57:    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
58:    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
59:  }
60:}
61:public class SaveOwner {
62:  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
63:    repository.save(owner);
64:  }
65:}
66:public class RespondWithOwner {
67:  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
68:    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
69:  }
70:}
71:```
72:
73:`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`
74:
75:```yaml
76:handle:
77:  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
78:```
79:
80:```java
81:public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
82:  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
83:      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
84:    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
85:  }
86:}
87:```
88:
89:### Step wiring
90:
91:Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
92:point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
93:method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
94:`method:`.
95:
96:- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
97:  as `@Parameter T`.
98:- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
99:  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
100:  branch; not calling it short-circuits.
101:
102:### Function parameters
103:
104:Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:
105:
106:- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
107:- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
108:- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
109:  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
110:  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
111:- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
112:  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.
113:
114:### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`
115:
116:Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
117:into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):
118:
119:- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
120:- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
121:  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
122:- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
123:  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.
124:
125:### Naming
126:
127:Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
128:absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
129:publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
130:`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).
131:
132:Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
133:responder. Steps in between work with entities.
134:
135:### Request body and validation
136:
137:- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
138:  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
139:  first step publishes it as a variable.
140:- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
141:  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
142:  invalid body can return 400.
143:
144:### Transactions
145:
146:`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
147:listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
148:the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.
149:
150:### Errors
151:
152:Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
153:Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
154:`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
155:`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
156:anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.
157:
158:### Security
159:
160:Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:
161:
162:```yaml
163:composition:
164:  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
165:```
166:
167:- Full reference: https://officefloor.net/llms.txt

content.text:
I added a "Settle selected" button that settles all the ticked claims at once. All 4 tests in the bulk settle spec pass with `bin/e2e`.

It works the same way as the existing "Open selected" button:

- **Server:** a new `POST /api/sheets/{sheet}/claims/bulk-settle` endpoint (`BulkSettleClaims.java`, plus small request and response classes). It puts the selected claims in list order: people in the order they were added, newest claim first within a person. It then settles each one as the signed-in user, using the same code a single settle uses. So the closed-period rule, the rule that whoever opened a claim can't settle it, and the clerk limit all apply exactly as before.
  - A claim that goes to PENDING counts as settled.
  - A claim that can't be settled is left alone and counted as refused, as is a selected id the sheet doesn't have.
  - Each claim that goes through writes the same audit lines a single settle writes.
- **Screen:** a new panel in `features/claims/bulk-settle.slot.tsx`, placed right after the bulk-open panel. It shows how many were settled and how many refused (`bulk-settled`, `bulk-settle-refused`). It updates the claim list and clears the ticked boxes after it runs, and shows `bulk-settle-error` if the request itself fails.

No database change was needed.
